title: Graphical Exploration of the Period Parameter B in the General Sine Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Consider f(x) = A\sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{B}(x - C)\right) + D with A = 3 and C = D = 0, so f(x) = 3\sin(2\pi x / B). (a) Describe what happens to the graph of f(x) on [-4\pi, 4\pi] as B increases through positive values B = 1, 3, 2\pi, 5\pi. (b) Explain what happens to the graph for negative values of B, such as B = -3 and B = -2\pi.
finalAnswer: \text{(a) Increasing } B > 0 \text{ stretches the wave horizontally (longer wavelength, fewer cycles)}; \quad \text{(b) } B < 0 \text{ has period } |B| \text{ and reflects the graph across the } x\text{-axis}

steps.title: Write the Simplified Function for A = 3, C = D = 0
steps.explanation: Substituting A = 3, C = 0, and D = 0 yields a sine wave centered at the origin with amplitude 3 and fundamental period |B|.
steps.why: The distance required for (2*pi/|B|)*x to advance by 2*pi is |B|.

steps.title: Part (a): Effect of Increasing Positive Values of B
steps.explanation: As B increases from 1 to 3, 2*pi, and 5*pi, each oscillation takes a longer horizontal distance B to complete. Visually, the wave stretches horizontally away from the y-axis, and the number of complete waves visible in [-4*pi, 4*pi] decreases.
steps.why: Increasing B decreases the angular frequency 2*pi/B, which stretches the graph horizontally by factor B/(2*pi).

steps.title: Part (b): Effect of Negative Values of B
steps.explanation: Because sine is an odd function (sin(-u) = -sin(u)), replacing B = 3 or 2*pi with B = -3 or -2*pi keeps the period equal to |B| (3 or 2*pi) while reflecting the entire graph across the x-axis (or equivalently across the y-axis).
steps.why: By the odd symmetry of sine, negating the frequency coefficient negates the output of the function.
